results.title: Describing nonstationary data streams in the frequency domain
results.content: *Concept drift* remains one of the primary challenges for the data stream processing methods. This work proposes the *Frequency Filtering Metadescriptor* (ffm) – a method for unsupervised data stream characterization that extracts the most informative frequency components visible in the feature vector of each processed sample, approximated at the level of a data chunk. This work describes the *Frequency Filtering Metadescriptor* – a method that extracts a *metadescription* of a data stream using informative frequency components to describe changes in the processed concepts. The rest of the work is organized as follows: Section 2 describes the related works, focusing on the strategies of data stream metadescription used in the literature; Section 3 describes the method and expands on the intuition behind frequency analysis; Section 4 describes the design of experiments and their goals; Section 5 analyzes the obtained results; Section 6 presents the analysis of real-world insects data streams [10] using the proposed approach.

results.title: Describing Nonstationary Data Streams in Frequency Domain
results.content: Similarly to the approach adopted in the first experiment, the obtained representation was normalized and clustered with *k-means* to an actual number of concepts present in the data stream, equivalent to 4444 (number of drifts +11+1+ 1). The final experiment focused on the proposed ffm approach, evaluating its ability to describe the high-dimensional data streams by identifying the number of concepts present in the given period. For this purpose, the insects data streams [10] were analyzed in a framework following the processing scheme of (a) extracting the metadescription of a data stream with ffm (b) identifying of the number of concepts present in the stream based on k-means clustering and silhouette score maximization, and (c) separating the stream into specific concepts. The presented experiments showed that the proposed approach allows for concept identification competitive with the baseline of pca feature extraction and statistically significantly better than state-of-the-art adapted in the concept drift detection and data stream classification tasks.
